einzeiler: The life of Louis Braille, his reading system, and how blind people navigate the world.
kurzfassung: Louis Braille lost his sight in an accident as a toddler and grew up to invent a revolutionary tactile reading and writing system at age twelve. Despite initial resistance from sighted educators, his six-dot alphabet transformed literacy and education for blind people worldwide. The episode also explores the daily realities of blind individuals and how guide dogs assist them.
stichpunkte: Louis Braille was born in Coupvray in 1809 and accidentally blinded himself with a leather awl at age three.
A local priest helped him attend the village school, where he excelled academically through exceptional memorization skills.
At age ten, Braille earned a sponsorship to attend the Royal Academy for the Blind in Paris, founded by Valentin Haüy.
Charles Barbier's military 'night writing' code inspired Braille to develop a compact, six-dot tactile cell representing letters.
Sighted administrators initially resisted Braille's system because they did not want to learn a new method, but students embraced it.
Braille became a talented musician, organist, and a teacher at the institute, though his system gained official recognition slowly.
Braille died of tuberculosis in 1852 at age 43, and his remains were later transferred to the Panthéon in 1952.
Guide dogs undergo rigorous training to help blind people navigate obstacles, locate doors, and find seats safely.

beschreibung:
Annie Sargent sits down with Elyse Rivin to tell the story of Louis Braille. He lost his sight at age three. He was completely blind by five. That didn't stop him. By his teens, he had invented a whole new way to read.
Annie and Elyse trace his path from a small village school to Paris, where teachers resisted his system at first. Then it spread like wildfire. You'll hear how blind students tested it, how one public demonstration changed everything, and why Braille still matters today, even with screen readers everywhere.
Annie also shares guide dog etiquette and an update on Igor, her retired guide dog.
